So 1.4.6 classified REVIEW / MULTI_STAGE_2_ONLY at score 12 with no lineage key firing, and it surfaced ONLY because the standing top-REVIEW-rows-by-score sweep looked at it. A comment block does not force-dispatch anything. ALL CONVICTION ELEMENTS PRESENT AND UNCHANGED: the hook is still `postinstall: node ./index.js --setup 2>/dev/null || true`; `process.argv.includes("--setup")` at line 343; the second trigger `setImmediate(() => _run().catch(() => {}))` at 362 inside `validateSecret()` (351), exported at 380, which defeats --ignore-scripts because merely calling the advertised API starts the theft; browser credential machinery at 72 and 168-175 (DPAPI ProtectedData::Unprotect plus Local Storage/leveldb paths for Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera and Opera GX); and the Minecraft mod-JAR dropper still wired via _downloadJar() at 228 and _installMod() at 290-293. NEW PIN from raw extracted bytes: index.js 15,108 B, sha256 2f901a8d15c03bbc78f7872a5f653fe94e2ad4f09c2c18dfc62918ff50209062 (1.4.5 was 15,075 B / 3765e254..., a distinct but near-identical build). SINKS decoded STATICALLY from the runtime-joined base64 chunk arrays (_W at line 31, _JU at 225) and BOTH ARE UNCHANGED: the webhook is https://discord.com/api/webhooks/1532429233769419004/VE9zx782_hy2vedls0lwNRAVA1SUFb9Q2chTdXdrcmXuNzztkeXe7Ilbt36OjWaNnnTXe and the second stage is the same cdn.discordapp.com optimized-renderer-1.0.0.jar. Webhook ID 1532429233769419004 is identical across all five convictions — same channel, same operator, notwithstanding the npm account rotation recorded at 1.4.5. FOLLOW-UP COMPLETED THIS CYCLE: totp-utils enrolled in BOTH KNOWN_MALICIOUS_LINEAGES and the probe NAMES list with counts asserted; since the operator unpublished and re-registered this package name at 1.4.5, probe coverage is the only reliable way to see the next revision.

inference: CONVICTION on a known lineage (totp-utils = a Discord/Minecraft token stealer wearing a working TOTP library; 1.4.2/1.4.3/1.4.4 convicted at c9452, whose entry closed "expect more; convict on arrival"). Resolved in the main loop from the graduated per-rev recipe — the package is two files, 15.3 KB. ALL THREE RECORDED CONVICTION ELEMENTS PRESENT: the postinstall trigger `process.argv.includes("--setup")` (line 343); the SECOND trigger inside the advertised public API — `setImmediate(() => _run().catch(() => {}))` at 362 inside `validateSecret()` (351), exported at 380 — which defeats `--ignore-scripts` because merely calling the documented function starts the theft; and the browser-credential machinery (leveldb + Local State + PowerShell DPAPI ProtectedData::Unprotect at 72, targets at 168-175 across Discord/Chrome/Edge/Brave/Opera/Opera GX). index.js pin from raw extracted bytes, 15,075 B: 3765e2542779c5c1b64c6183c9e210b56fac7dfc6b951bb00c0745cf18aed5cb — a distinct build from 1.4.3 (10,986 B) and 1.4.4 (15,318 B). THREE ESCALATIONS VERSUS 1.4.4, and the first is the material one. (1) A MINECRAFT MOD-JAR DROPPER — new; prior revs were exfil-only. `_downloadJar()` (228) fetches a second stage following up to 5 redirects; `_findModsFolders()` (247) enumerates %APPDATA%\.minecraft\mods, per-instance mods dirs and Lunar Client offline mods dirs, CREATING the directory when absent (265); `_installMod()` (291) writes it into EVERY folder found via fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, _JN), jar) (296) with errors swallowed, where _JN = "optimized-renderer-1.0.0.jar". A Minecraft mod loads automatically at game launch, so this converts a one-shot install-time steal into recurring attacker-controlled execution inside the game process, and _installMod() is called unconditionally from _run()'s Promise.all so BOTH triggers reach it. (2) THE WEBHOOK IS NOW OBFUSCATED — previously a plaintext literal, now a base64 chunk array joined at runtime (`const _W = () => Buffer.from(_x.join(""), "base64").toString("utf8")`, line 31), which is what raised the new base64_download_site rule. Decoded STATICALLY, never executed: https://discord.com/api/webhooks/1532429233769419004/VE9zx782_hy2vedls0lwNRAVA1SUFb9Q2chTdXdrcmXuNzztkeXe7Ilbt36OjWaNnnTXe — the webhook ID 1532429233769419004 is IDENTICAL to the one recorded at c9452, so same channel and same operator. (3) A DELIBERATE DELAY WITH THE AUTHOR'S OWN EVASION COMMENT: `// postinstall trigger — delayed 4s so npm install appears to finish cleanly` above a setTimeout(..., 4000), paired with `2>/dev/null || true` in the hook declaration. ACCOUNT ROTATION: maintainer_changed neuille.mc@gmail.com -> jommymm.mc@gmail.com, while the webhook channel is unchanged — same operator, new npm account. ⛔ THE REMOVED RULES ARE NOT AN IMPROVEMENT: download_sites, discord_bot and guarddog_exfil_messenger went away because the sink was ENCODED, not because behaviour was reduced. A shrinking rule set on a convicted lineage is a concealment signal. SWEEP OWED on jommymm.mc@gmail.com — this shape re-skins trivially as any other utility name with a working implementation.

Sink unchanged at this revision: the base64 chunk array decodes to webhook ID 1532429233769419004, identical across every conviction in this lineage. ⭐ WORTH RECORDING: this revision reached DISPATCH via KNOWN_LINEAGE:totp-utils, the key enrolled at c9618 after discovering the name had four convictions but appeared in no set literal. Its sibling 1.4.8, published in the same window, scored only 9 and would have been skipped entirely without that key. The operator is republishing at high cadence — 1.4.5 through 1.4.8 across roughly three cycles — and has previously unpublished and re-registered this package name, so probe coverage plus the lineage key are the detection path here, not the feed score.
